'''Philip E. Mason''' is a British [[chemist]] and [[YouTuber]] with the online pseudonym '''Thunderf00t''' (also '''VoiceOfThunder'''). He is best known for his critiques of [[religion]], [[pseudoscience]] and [[creationism]]. He works at the [[Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry]] of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].

==Early life==
Mason received a [[BSc]] (2:1) (1993) and [[PhD]] (1997) in [[chemistry]] from the [[University of Birmingham]].<ref name="CZ">{{cite web |title=Phil Mason |url=http://www.uochb.cz/web/structure/268.html?do%5BloadData%5D=1&itemKey=en_32 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306052740/http://www.uochb.cz/web/structure/268.html?do%5bloadData%5d=1&itemKey=en_32 |archive-date=6 March 2019 |access-date=10 March 2014 |publisher=[[Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic]]}}</ref> From 2003<ref>{{cite journal|last=Mason|first=P. E.|author2=Neilson, G. W. |author3=Dempsey, C. E. |author4=Barnes, A. C. |author5= Cruickshank, J. M. |title=The hydration structure of guanidinium and thiocyanate ions: Implications for protein stability in aqueous solution|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=8 April 2003|volume=100|issue=8|pages=4557–4561|doi=10.1073/pnas.0735920100 |pmid=12684536 |pmc=404697|bibcode=2003PNAS..100.4557M|doi-access=free}}</ref> until at least August 2010, Mason was affiliated with the [[University of Bristol]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/biochemistry/news/archive/2010/aug10.html | title=News | publisher=University of Bristol | date=August 2010 | access-date=22 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140324064538/http://www.bristol.ac.uk/biochemistry/news/archive/2010/aug10.html|archive-date=24 March 2014}}</ref>

==Career==
Mason worked at [[Cornell University]]'s department of food science from 2002 until 2012, where he studied the molecular interactions between water and sugar molecules,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://impact.cals.cornell.edu/project/experimental-molecular-dynamics-studies-water-structuring-sugars |title=Experimental molecular dynamics studies of water structuring by sugars |access-date=26 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907165120/https://impact.cals.cornell.edu/project/experimental-molecular-dynamics-studies-water-structuring-sugars |archive-date=7 September 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> as well as molecular modeling with regard to proteins and [[guanidinium]] solutions. As of 2025, he was working at the Institute of [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] and [[Biochemistry]] of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic]] as a member of a research group headed by [[Pavel Jungwirth]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prague |first=IOCB |title=Phil Mason |url=https://www.uochb.cz/en/directory/103/phil-mason |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=IOCB Prague |language=en}}</ref>

===Alkali metals research===
Mason, on his own and with some fellow technical workers, did original physical chemistry research into the nature of the [[alkali metal]]s ([[sodium]] and [[potassium]], for example) and their chemistry with [[oxygen]] and [[water]].<ref name="Bell">{{Cite journal|last=Bell|first=Philip|date=26 January 2015|title=News: Sodium's explosive secrets revealed |quote=The spectacular reaction of alkali metals with water was poorly understood despite being a staple of chemistry classes. |url=https://www.nature.com/news/sodium-s-explosive-secrets-revealed-1.16771 |journal=Nature |doi=10.1038/nature.2015.16771}}</ref> It has been known since the metals could be obtained in pure forms that they are explosive when dropped into water. It has long been thought this was caused by the [[dissociation (chemistry)|dissociation]] of water by the metal, releasing [[hydrogen]] and oxygen which recombined in an explosion.  Mason developed experimental methods and results that indicate the first reaction of alkali metals and water was [[Coulomb's Law|coulombic]] (that is, electrical charge forces) in nature which shatters and drives the metal in an extremely pure state into the water, causing both further coulombic and water dissociation. This result, developed in 2015, was completely new to chemistry.<ref name="Bell"/> His co-authored research was published in the journal ''[[Nature Chemistry]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mason |first1=Philip E. |last2=Uhlig |first2=Frank |last3=Vaněk |first3=Václav |last4=Buttersack |first4=Tillmann |last5=Bauerecker |first5=Sigurd |last6=Jungwirth |first6=Pavel |author-link6=Pavel Jungwirth |date=26 January 2015 |title=Coulomb explosion during the early stages of the reaction of alkali metals with water |journal=[[Nature Chemistry]] |language=en |volume=7 |issue=3 |pages=250–4 |doi=10.1038/nchem.2161 |pmid=25698335 |bibcode=2015NatCh...7..250M |issn=1755-4330}}</ref>

On 5 June 2020, his co-authored research on [[solvated electron]]s dissolved in ammonia was published in the science journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Buttersack |first1=Tillman |last2=Mason |first2=Phillip E. |last3=McMullen |first3=Ryan S. |last4=Schewe |first4=H. Christian |last5=Martinek |first5=Tomas |last6=Jungwirth |first6=Pavel |author-link6=Pavel Jungwirth |date=5 June 2020 |title=Photoelectron spectra of alkali metal–ammonia microjets: From blue electrolyte to bronze metal |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaz7607 |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |volume=368 |issue=6495 |pages=1086–91 |doi=10.1126/science.aaz7607 |pmid=32499436 |bibcode=2020Sci...368.1086B |access-date=7 June 2020|hdl=2433/254491 |s2cid=219312089 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Online activities==
Mason produces [[YouTube]] videos under the pseudonym Thunderf00t.<ref name="Farrelly">{{cite news |last1=Farrelly |first1=Elizabeth |title=Highways of future, where solar panels change our world |publisher=[[Sydney Morning Herald]] |date=9 June 2014|id={{ProQuest|1536863134}} }}</ref> A 2012 journal article stated that Thunderf00t's channel and [[P.Z. Myers]]' blog were "among the two most popular secularist hubs online."<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=Christopher |last2=Cimino |first2=Richard |date=2012-02-21 |title=Atheisms Unbound: The Role of the New Media in the Formation of a Secularist Identity |journal=Secularism and Nonreligion |language=en |volume=1 |pages=17 |doi=10.5334/snr.ab |issn=2053-6712 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Mason has used his online persona to critically examine a range of topics, including proposals to build roads [[Solar Roadways|surfaced with glass solar panels]].<ref name="Farrelly"/> He has also criticised [[Elizabeth Holmes]], [[Anita Sarkeesian]],<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://gamesbeat.com/critic-anita-sarkeesian-receives-online-death-threats-after-latest-feminist-frequency-video-on-games/ |title=Critic Anita Sarkeesian receives online death threats after latest Feminist Frequency video on games |date=2014-08-27 |work=VentureBeat |access-date=2018-09-07 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newstatesman.com/future-proof/2014/08/tropes-vs-anita-sarkeesian-passing-anti-feminist-nonsense-critique |title=Tropes vs Anita Sarkeesian: on passing off anti-feminist nonsense as critique |date=2014-08-27 |work=New Statesman |access-date=2018-09-07 |language=en}}</ref> and [[Elon Musk]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.inverse.com/article/30830-how-realistic-hyperloop-one-us-map |title=How Realistic Is This Hyperloop One Future Map of the U.S.? |last=Brown |first=Mike |date=2017-04-27 |work=Inverse |access-date=2018-09-07 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.westword.com/news/hyperloop-one-and-importance-of-tunnels-9555475 |title=The One Thing Hyperloop Must Do to Avoid Becoming a Disaster |last=Roberts |first=Michael |date=2017-11-20 |work=Westword |access-date=2018-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://nationalinterest.org/feature/hyperloop-projects-may-be-uniquely-vulnerable-terrorism-21781 |title=Hyperloop Projects May Be Uniquely Vulnerable to Terrorism |last=Pring-Mill |first=David |date=2017-08-03 |work=The National Interest |access-date=2018-09-07 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Hje7h_WVkY |title=Elon Musk: 3 years to Bankruptcy |language=en |access-date=2024-05-02 |via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

In 2015, Jenny Keller, who ran the YouTube channel "Laughing Witch", attempted to get Mason fired by sending letters to his employer. Keller stated that these efforts were intended to pressure Mason to change what she considered sexist and islamophobic content on his channel. After promoting the campaign online, Mason responded by posting a series of videos scrutinizing Keller and the [[Bowie, Maryland]]-based company she runs with her husband, Porcelain Tub Restoration. These videos led to many of Mason's fans posting negative reviews online for that company.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.wusa9.com/article/news/local/bowie/prince-georges-co-business-battles-economic-cyber-terrorism/202654220 |title=Prince George's Co. business battles  |date=2015-10-30 |work=WUSA |access-date=2018-09-07 |language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908015702/https://www.wusa9.com/article/news/local/bowie/prince-georges-co-business-battles-economic-cyber-terrorism/202654220 |archive-date=2018-09-08 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On several occasions, Mason has made guest appearances on the ''[[Drunken Peasants|Drunken Peasants Podcast]]''.<ref>{{Citation|last=Drunken Peasants|title=Drunken Peasants Podcast Special Guest: ThunderF00t - ThunderF00t Meets G-Man - Much More! DPP #29|date=2014-06-06|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_SSFd1I6KUM|access-date=2019-07-06}}</ref>

In July 2020, Mason had several of his videos on YouTube debunking [[COVID-19 misinformation|COVID-19 conspiracy theories]] falsely flagged and taken down.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Greenspan |first1=Rachel E. |last2=Tenbarge |first2=Kat |date=2020-09-26 |title=YouTubers' channels and videos are being mistakenly deleted for debunking COVID-19 conspiracy theories |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/youtube-demonetized-covid-19-disinformation-moderation-automation-bots-strikes-2020-9 |access-date=2021-02-11 |work=[[Insider Inc.|Insider]] |via=}}</ref>

===Creationism===
Through his YouTube account Thunderf00t, Mason produced a series of videos titled "Why do people laugh at creationists?", focusing primarily on [[Kent Hovind]]'s arguments in public seminars. [[Sociologist]] Richard Cimino has described the tone of these videos as "that of the professional, well-educated, and articulate British academic expert exposing—in voiceover—the irrational behavior and attitudes of the believer."<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oVBjBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA99 |title=Atheist Awakening: Secular Activism and Community in America | publisher=Oxford University Press| author=Cimino, Richard | year=2014 | pages=99|isbn=9780199986323 }}</ref> Mason (originally known only as Thunderf00t) debated with VenomFangX, a YouTube blogger who supports [[creationism]], in a series of public exchanges that lasted almost two years. The series also covered other creationists, such as [[Ray Comfort]] and intelligent design proponent Casey Luskin.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.csicop.org/si/show/skepticism_via_youtube/|title=Skepticism via YouTube| work=[[Skeptical Inquirer]]|date=November–December 2009|access-date=2 April 2014|first=Tim |last=Farley|author-link=Tim Farley}}</ref>
